subject: re-def
title: RE.DEF.------PROG.CONT.
description: Diagram in EXT.F(II)-6, paired with v1-p444-1. (C)RE-DIF (the concept of redefinitions) is crossed with PROG-CONT (progressional continuance). VT-DY (vibrational dynamics) → RE-DIF and MT-INTR (multiple interpretation) → RE-DIF; APP-RDEF (applied redefinitions) → RE-DIF, with APP-RDEF also → POL-P (political policies). RE-DIF → PROG-CONT (the crossing) → AFL-DY (affinity dynamics). A separate sub-chain: SOC-RT-DY (social reality dynamics) → AF-CON (affinity convergence) → LANG-DY (language dynamics) → ALT-F (alternative functionalism). Structural argument: the concept of redefinitions is over-determined upstream by *three* parallel feeds (vibrational dynamics, multiple interpretation, applied redefinitions). Applied redefinitions also feeds political policies as a sibling output. The redefinitions → progressional continuance → affinity dynamics chain is the productive line. The parallel social-reality-dynamics → affinity-convergence → language-dynamics → alternative-functionalism chain runs structurally separate, with no convergence into the main redefinitions chain. The diagram thus stages the seventies' diagnostic claim: the *concept* of redefinitions is well-fed and productive of progressional continuance and affinity dynamics, but the social-reality-driven alternative functionalism chain runs in a different track — meaning institutional acknowledgment of the music in the seventies (per the prose) does not automatically channel into alternative functionalism. The two productive chains run in parallel without convergence.
